purpose: Phase 4 (Experiments A and B) evidence for the diabetes-brfss-v2 85%-accuracy investigation. These are NOT freshly re-run in this task -- they are the existing, already-saved outputs of ml_pipeline/diabetes/train_brfss_v2.py's own model-family comparison and hyperparameter search, produced with the identical 14-feature v2 dataset, identical StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) protocol, and identical scale_pos_weight. Re-running them would be redundant (same seed, same data, same deterministic algorithms) -- they are cited here, not fabricated, and their source files are named explicitly below so they can be independently re-verified.
source_files: ml_pipeline/diabetes/reports/v2_final_recommendation.md (v1-vs-v2, i.e. the 21-feature 'use every available BRFSS column' configuration)

experiment_A_hyperparameter_tuning.method: RandomizedSearchCV, 20 candidate configurations, cv=3, scoring=roc_auc, training split only; winning configuration re-verified with a full 5-fold StratifiedKFold
experiment_A_hyperparameter_tuning.conclusion: Hyperparameter tuning moved CV ROC-AUC by 0.0007 (0.8130 -> 0.8137) -- this is already the configuration deployed as diabetes-brfss-v2. A gain this small cannot plausibly bridge the ~0.20 accuracy gap needed to reach 85% at a sensitivity-preserving threshold; the OOF sweep in threshold_analysis.json (this same directory) already uses these exact tuned hyperparameters and still requires threshold>=0.45 (sensitivity 0.23) to cross 85%.

experiment_B_model_family_comparison.method: 5-fold StratifiedKFold CV, training split only, same 14-feature dataset, default/near-default hyperparameters per family
experiment_B_model_family_comparison.note_on_accuracy_column: cross_validate's 'accuracy' scorer uses each model's default 0.5 decision threshold, NOT the tuned/calibrated 0.10 threshold used in production -- shown here specifically because it answers the 85%-accuracy question directly: even at the threshold each model would naturally choose, none approach 85%.
experiment_B_model_family_comparison.highest_cv_accuracy_family: random_forest (0.7383, still 11.2 points below the 85% target, at its own default threshold)
experiment_B_model_family_comparison.highest_cv_roc_auc_family: hist_gradient_boosting (0.8131), statistically indistinguishable from xgboost_default (0.8130) -- within fold-to-fold noise
experiment_B_model_family_comparison.conclusion: All four evaluated families cluster within a narrow band (CV ROC-AUC 0.796-0.813; CV accuracy at default threshold 0.705-0.738). None comes remotely close to 85% accuracy, and switching families would not change the fundamental accuracy/sensitivity tradeoff documented in threshold_analysis.json, since that tradeoff is driven by class imbalance (~15% positive prevalence) and the achievable ROC-AUC ceiling (~0.81), not by which family is used.

experiment_C_feature_configuration.method: Not re-run as a new experiment -- diabetes-brfss-v1 (already trained, evaluated, and documented) IS the 'use every legitimate BRFSS column' configuration: all 21 original features, including the 7 removed for v2 (Income, Education, AnyHealthcare, NoDocbcCost, MentHlth, PhysHlth, Veggies).
experiment_C_feature_configuration.conclusion: Using every available legitimate BRFSS feature (v1, 21 columns) raises test ROC-AUC by only 0.0019 over v2's 14-column set. No fabricated feature (family history, HbA1c, fasting glucose) was added, and none may legitimately be added -- BRFSS does not collect them (see docs/ml/diabetes/limitations.md and ml_pipeline/diabetes/reports/family_history_investigation.md). Feature configuration is not the lever that would close the gap to 85% accuracy.

overall_conclusion: Across every legitimate BRFSS-based lever already evidenced in this repository -- hyperparameter tuning (Experiment A), model family choice (Experiment B), and feature configuration (Experiment C, i.e. v1's full 21-feature set) -- achievable test-set ROC-AUC is bounded within approximately 0.796-0.820. At this discrimination ceiling and ~15% positive class prevalence, no legitimate threshold or model choice can reach 85% accuracy without sensitivity collapsing to roughly 15-25% (see threshold_analysis.json and final_comparison.json in this directory). This is a property of the available data and achievable discrimination, not of insufficient tuning effort.
